title: “Monks, I will teach you nine things rooted in craving. Listen and pay close attention. And what, monks, are the nine things rooted in craving?…
content: “Monks, I will teach you nine things rooted in craving. Listen and pay close attention. And what, monks, are the nine things rooted in craving? Dependent on craving, seeking arises; dependent on seeking, gain arises; dependent on gain, decision arises; dependent on decision, desire and lust arise; dependent on desire and lust, attachment arises; dependent on attachment, possessiveness arises; dependent on possessiveness, guarding arises; dependent on guarding, the taking up of sticks and swords, quarrels, disputes, arguments, slander, false speech, and many evil, unwholesome states arise. These, monks, are the nine things rooted in craving.”

title: “Monks, if a monk, reflecting thus, knows: ‘I dwell much with a greedy mind; I dwell much with a hateful mind; I dwell much with…
content: “Monks, if a monk, reflecting thus, knows: ‘I dwell much with a greedy mind; I dwell much with a hateful mind; I dwell much with a mind overcome by sloth and torpor; I dwell much with restlessness; I dwell much with doubt; I dwell much with anger; I dwell much with a defiled mind; I dwell much with bodily fever; I dwell much with laziness; I dwell much unconcentrated’ — then that monk should make a strong wish, arouse effort, be energetic, strive, be strong-minded, not fall away, be mindful and clearly comprehending for the abandonment of those evil, unwholesome states. Just as, monks, if a turban or head were on fire, one would make a strong wish, arouse effort, be energetic, strive, be strong-minded, not fall away, be mindful and clearly comprehending to extinguish that turban or head — so too, that monk should make a strong wish … for the abandonment of those evil, unwholesome states.”

title: “And how, monks, is there non-restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached to agreeable forms and repelled…
content: “And how, monks, is there non-restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached to agreeable forms and repelled by disagreeable forms. He dwells with bodily mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. Thus, monks, is non-restraint.”

title: “And what, Ānanda, is the path, the way leading to the abandoning of the five lower fetters? Here, Ānanda, a monk, by the relinquishment of…
content: “And what, Ānanda, is the path, the way leading to the abandoning of the five lower fetters? Here, Ānanda, a monk, by the relinquishment of attachments (upadhiviveka), by the abandoning of unwholesome states, by the complete calming of bodily coarseness, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.”

title: (Calā): Having been born, one must die, Seeing suffering in birth, Fetters and afflictions — Therefore I do not delight in birth. The Buddha has…
content:
(Calā):
Having been born, one must die,
Seeing suffering in birth,
Fetters and afflictions —
Therefore I do not delight in birth.
The Buddha has taught the Dhamma
That leads beyond renewed existence,
Abolishing all suffering —
He has established me in truth.
Beings headed for the form realm,
Those aspiring to the formless realm,
If they do not know cessation,
They go to renewed existence.

title: “Householder, just as a house with a badly thatched roof — the ridgepole is not protected, the rafters are not protected, the walls are not…
content: “Householder, just as a house with a badly thatched roof — the ridgepole is not protected, the rafters are not protected, the walls are not protected; the ridgepole becomes soaked and leaks, the rafters become soaked and leak, the walls become soaked and leak; the ridgepole rots, the rafters rot, the walls rot. So too, householder, when the mind is not guarded, bodily actions are not guarded, verbal actions … mental actions … then bodily actions become soaked with greed and leak, verbal actions become soaked with greed and leak, mental actions become soaked with greed and leak. For one whose bodily actions are soaked and leak with greed, whose verbal and mental actions are soaked and leak with greed, bodily actions rot, verbal actions rot, mental actions rot. For one whose bodily, verbal, and mental actions rot, death is not good, the end is not good.”

title: Life is swept along, The lifespan is short — Led to old age, There is no shelter. Seeing this danger in death, Always do meritorious…
content:
Life is swept along,
The lifespan is short —
Led to old age,
There is no shelter.
Seeing this danger in death,
Always do meritorious deeds
That bring true happiness.
Here, restraint of body,
Restraint of speech and mind —
One who does this, even while dying,
Experiences happiness,
Because while still alive,
He has made merit.

title: “Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind…
content: “Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — regarding them, my mind becomes inflamed when they are present, and diminishes when they are future, not yet attained.’ Then, monks, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — regarding them, for my own benefit, I will dwell heedful, protecting my mind with mindfulness.’ Therefore, monks, regarding the five strands of sensual pleasure that your minds formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — your minds become inflamed when they are present, and diminish when they are future, not yet attained. Therefore, monks, regarding the five strands of sensual pleasure that your minds formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — for your own benefit, dwell heedful, protecting your minds with mindfulness.”

title: All formations are impermanent, Having arisen, they must cease; Having arisen, they are subject to cessation, Their calming is bliss.
content:
All formations are impermanent,
Having arisen, they must cease;
Having arisen, they are subject to cessation,
Their calming is bliss.

title: “Monks, those ascetics or brahmins who do not know as it actually is the gratification as gratification, the peril as peril, the escape as escape…
content: “Monks, those ascetics or brahmins who do not know as it actually is the gratification as gratification, the peril as peril, the escape as escape in the case of forms — they will certainly not understand forms as they actually are, nor can they lead others to a similar position, namely, understanding forms as they actually are — such a thing is not possible. Monks, those ascetics or brahmins who know as it actually is the gratification as gratification, the peril as peril, the escape as escape in the case of forms — they will certainly understand forms as they actually are, and they can lead others to a similar position, namely, understanding forms as they actually are — such a thing is possible.”
